subject: Re: BlueHarbor DPA — Incident notification window & subprocessor cooperation
messages:
From: Liam Harris <liam.harris@blueharbor.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@blueharbor.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BlueHarbor DPA — notification timing + subprocessor cooperation

Connor / Marissa — thanks for sending the draft DPA (attached). BlueHarbor legal and security have two items we need to close before we circulate internally:

1) Incident notification timing: we typically push for 48-hour initial notification for incidents involving customer-identifiable data. Your draft lists 72 hours — can you confirm Redwood's rationale and whether you can commit to 48 hours in material incidents?

2) Subprocessor cooperation & evidence transfer: we need clarity on how your subprocessors will be engaged during investigations, and what evidence/export timelines look like for cross-border requests. Specifically:
   - Will Redwood require subprocessor consent before transferring forensic data?
   - Can you commit to an attestable list of subprocessors and an operational contact for each?

Attached: our internal security checklist for DPAs and a short summary of our regulatory constraints. Can we get Redwood's position in writing and a redline? We can also schedule a short legal call this week.

Thanks — Liam
Liam Harris
Director, Security Partnerships
BlueHarbor Financial
Attachments: BlueHarbor_DPA_checklist.pdf (pdf), BH_reg_constraints.docx (docx)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Harris <liam.harris@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor DPA — notification timing + subprocessor cooperation

Liam — appreciate the clear asks and the checklist. High level position from Redwood: we recognize BlueHarbor's 48-hour preference for material incidents. Our standard operational constraints are: initial detection/triage windows (we need to validate scope and avoid false positives), and forensic evidence collection that sometimes requires coordination with subprocessors and external vendors. Below are our proposed positions for negotiation (redline attached).

Key points: 
- Initial notification: Redwood can commit to notifying BlueHarbor within 48 hours for confirmed material incidents that impact customer-identifiable data in production. For suspected incidents that require preliminary triage, we propose a 72-hour "initial awareness" notification with an explicit follow-up within 7 calendar days with findings.

- Detailed report & evidence: we will provide a preliminary incident report within 7 calendar days after confirmation, and a full technical report and evidence package within 30 calendar days where feasible. Where collection requires third-party cooperation (subprocessors), timelines may extend; we will log and communicate those dependencies in the preliminary report.

- Subprocessor cooperation: Redwood maintains a living subprocessor matrix (see attached). We will provide BlueHarbor with an attestation of subprocessors used for this account and assign an operational liaison per major subprocessor for evidence coordination. Redwood cannot unilaterally compel a subprocessor to export data beyond what their contract permits; we will use contractual channels and escalation to obtain exports, and where not possible, we will provide alternative forensic artifacts (snapshots, logs, hashes) to satisfy BlueHarbor's reasonable requests.

- Cross-border transfers: where export would trigger cross-border transfer constraints, Redwood will: 1) notify BlueHarbor of the constraint as soon as known, 2) propose an alternate evidence transfer plan (e.g., in-country review or redacted extracts), and 3) document the legal basis for any transfer.

- Good-faith cooperation clause: we are prepared to add a clause committing to "reasonable efforts" cooperation with BlueHarbor's investigators and to escalate to executive channels if subprocessors delay beyond a mutually agreed SLA.

Next steps: Marissa / Kimberly / Ben — please review the redline (DPA_redlines_v3.pdf) for tighter legal language and any obligations we should tighten before returning to BlueHarbor. Liam — if this direction is acceptable in principle, let's lock a 45-minute legal + security call Wednesday 3/3 or Thursday 3/4.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Security & Privacy Liaison
Redwood Inference
Attachments: DPA_redlines_v3.pdf (pdf), subprocessor_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor DPA — internal ops feasibility

Quick operational notes from the IR side:
- 48h for confirmed material incidents is doable, provided we have a clear definition of "material" in the contract (e.g., confirmed exposure of customer-identifiable data affecting > X customers or confirmed exfiltration). Otherwise we risk noisy churn.
- Recommend allowing 72-96h for initial triage cadence if the incident requires forensic engagement with multiple subprocessors; we can promise accelerated updates during that window.
- For subprocessors: we can assign liaisons and prioritize exports for customers on Dedicated/Private plans; for shared-hosted customers, we may be constrained by subprocessor contracts and capacity. Suggest we offer an "expedited export" add-on for BlueHarbor as a commercial option.

I'll add inline comments to DPA_redlines_v3 and the subprocessor matrix.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Lead Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@blueharbor.com>

Connor / Ben — thanks for the quick reply and the redline. A few points from BlueHarbor legal: 

- 48-hour initial notice is our baseline for material incidents; 72-hour awareness windows introduce ambiguity we cannot accept without stronger guardrails. Can you accept 48 hours for any incident that meets the attached definition of "material"? (see BH_material_def.docx)

- Subprocessor assurance: we require contractual assurances that Redwood will obtain the necessary consents from subprocessors to allow forensic exports when requested under this DPA, or in lieu of that, a binding commitment from Redwood to provide functionally equivalent artifacts within the same timelines.

- Audit evidence: please provide your most recent SOC 2 Type II report or arrange a confined review; we need this before final execution.

Would also like to see the names / roles of the operational liaisons you propose. We are available for the call Wednesday 3/3 11:00am PT.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@blueharbor.com>; Liam Harris <liam.harris@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-05T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor DPA — incident notification window & subprocessor cooperation (proposal)

Asha / Liam — thanks for the replies and the BH material definition. After internal review we've drafted a compromise redline that we believe addresses BlueHarbor's need for certainty while keeping realistic operational SLAs. Summary of the compromise positions (see attached DPA_redlines_v3 for full text):

1) Definition & trigger: adopt BlueHarbor's materiality definition (BH_material_def) as the contractual trigger for the 48-hour initial notification. We accept that if the incident meets that definition, Redwood will provide initial written notification within 48 hours of confirmation.

2) Suspected incidents: for events that do not meet the materiality trigger but are reasonably suspected, Redwood will send an "awareness" notice within 72 hours and commit to a status update within 7 calendar days.

3) Evidence & subprocessors: Redwood will provide an attested subprocessor list for the BlueHarbor account and name operational liaisons for the top-tier subprocessors within 5 business days after execution. Forcing exports from subprocessors where not contractually permitted remains infeasible; instead Redwood will contractually commit to provide functionally equivalent forensic artifacts within the same timeline, and to escalate to executive channels (documented escalation ladder) if cooperation is delayed beyond agreed SLAs.

4) Cross-border: where legal constraints prevent direct export, Redwood will propose an in-country review or redacted artifact transfer and document the legal basis.

5) Audit evidence: we'll provide a copy of our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; Marissa will coordinate the exchange.

Next steps: Marissa will circulate the redline and a short summary of the liaison roster. Ben will price an "expedited export" commercial option to cover prioritized subprocessor engagement if BlueHarbor wants guaranteed exports. If BlueHarbor agrees with the compromise in principle, we'll confirm the call for Wednesday 3/3 at 11:00am PT (calendar invite sent separately).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Connor O'Brien
Security & Privacy Liaison
Redwood Inference
Attachments: DPA_redlines_v3.pdf (pdf), incident_playbook_summary.docx (docx), subprocessor_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
